newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa gets $84 mln loan for tankers.
newsitem.headline: Formosa gets $84 mln loan for tankers.

text.p: Formosa Plastics Marine Corp, a unit of Taiwan's Formosa Plastics Group, said on Tuesday it had agreed with foreign banks to borrow US$84 million in syndicated loans for three newly ordered chemical tankers.
"Several foreign banks have agreed to offer US$84 million in syndicated loans to us to be used to buy three chemical tankers," a Formosa Marine official said by telephone.
The seven-year loan will bear a lending rate of SIBOR plus 0.425 percentage points, he said.
Bank of America of the United States and Sumitomo Bank of Japan are lead underwriters, he said.
The group has eight 30,000-tonne-class chemical tankers to transport chemical materials between Taiwan and the United States, where it has subsidiaries, he said.
The tankers also transport chemical materials for other companies, the official said.
"We had recently signed contracts to build three more 30,000-tonne-class chemical tankers, valued at a total of US$84 million," he said.

The group said last week it would invest some T$12 billion (US$436 million) to build six to eight very large crude oil carriers to meet demand from its US$9 billion petrochemical complex project, which is still under construction.
Each crude carrier will be in the 200,000-tonne class.
The group launched the massive project, including its sixth naphtha cracker and first full-fledged oil refinery, in 1993 in central Taiwan.

Construction will take six years and, once complete, will enable Formosa to break the longtime petroleum monopoly of state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp, which itself is being privatised to better cope with competition.
Formosa group has three key members: Formosa Plastics, Nan Ya Plastics and Formosa Chemical and Fiber.
